Elderflower Strawberry Macarons

Time: fucklong, like 3h or a day if you age your whites
Servings: 2-3 trays
Source: https://nickskitchen.com/french-macarons-recipe/, Sandy
Tags: tested, sweet, dessert, elaborate, vegetarian, gluten-free

This is a recipe to celebrate the season of strawberries and elderflower. It’s elaborate, highly technical, and a work in proggress.

Elderflower-strawberry reduction

Ingredients

  • 220g strawberries
  • 2-3 fresh elderflowers
  • 10ml lime juice
  • 30ml water
  • 1-2 tablespoons sugar

Instructions

Clean and dry off the elderflower and remove as much of the green parts as possible. You want to end with 6g of blooms.
Clean and cut strawberries into small pieces. Place into a pan with water, lime juice and 3g of the elderflowers. Bring to a simmer, medium heat, bring to a simmer stirring occasionally. Add sugar to taste. Simmer and stir until the fruit breaks down and gets mushy and jam like. Easily 15min+
When you’re happy with the consistency, remove it from heat and let it cool down a bit. Stir in the remaining blooms. Let it sit until it cools down more.
Push the mixture through a sieve with a spatula or a wooden spoon; You need to pass as much of it as possible, excluding the blooms and most of the seeds. Pick a sieve size that will not make you hate existing.
Stir the result, pour in a piping bag and stick it into fridge until you’re ready to use it.

White chocolate ganache

To be perfected

Ingredients

  • 50g heavy cream
  • 75g White chocolate
  • 15g Elderflowers, or more

Instructions

Day ahead:
Clean and dry the elderflowers, remove as much of the green stems as possible to get the desired amount of blooms. Put the blooms in a cup with heavy cream. Let steep in fridge overnight.
Chop the chocolate in a blender to get finer pieces. Put in a medium heat-proof bowl and stick it into microwave for just a bit (5s, mix, another 5s). It doesn’t have to melt, just get a bit warmer.
Heat the heavy cream with blooms in it, so that steam is rising from it, but it doesn’t boil (max 75°C). If you have the time, you can hold it at a lower temperature (~40°C) for a bit to steep first.
Strain the cream to remove the blooms and pour over the chocolate. Let it sit for a minte and then mix until combined. Cut a bit of cling film and place it directly on the chocolate to prevent a skin from forming. Let it cool down and then stick in the fridge for a few hours. For example until you make the macaron shells.
After it cools down, use a mixer with a whisk attachment to introduce air - whip it until it’s smooth, airy and lightens in colour.

Notes

2.5:1 dark chocolate to cream was too thick. Try 1:1 or 1.5:1
Dark chocolate is too overpowering. Try adding butter? Mascaropone? (made the macarons soggy) Switch to an entirely different filling? ✓ (White chocolate is the best) Steep elderflowers in cream? ✓
The macarons are behaving like a flower would. You can barely feel the elderflower when it’s cold from the fridge :( If you let it sit at room temperature for 5-10minutes, it comes out.

Macaron shells

Check the macarons recipe if unsure.

Ingredients

  • 105g egg whites, aged
  • 144g almond flour
  • 125g powdered sugar
  • 105g granulated sugar
  • lime zest, from 1/4 to 1/2 worth of limes

Instructions

Separate egg whites (cca 3 eggs) and cover with a towel. Let it sit out overnight or put in the microwave for 5s, three times.
Mix almond flour and powdered sugar, sift twice.
Sart whipping the egg whites on medium speed until they are foamy.
Wipe your spatula. Gradually add the granulated sugar, then switch to medium-high speed. Beat until the meringue is glossy and stiff. I like to scrape the sides with the spatula to make sure no undissolved sugar stays on the sides. The whipping can take anywhere from 3-7min depending on your mixer.
Medium speed, incorporate lime zest. They say switch to high speed for 30s, but I found the meringue satisfactory before that. Maybe it’s just to get it to fly off the whisk?
Wipe down a silicone baking mat, set it on a baking tray.
Sift the dry ingredients into the meringue. Mix them in, then switch to folding. This is the tricky part, you need to fold until the macronage flows off the spatula in ribbons (like thick lava) instead of falling off in chunks. The ribbons should also sit on top of it for ~10s instead of melting in. Go watch a few videos to understand the desired consistency. It’s better to undermix.
Prepare a piping bag with a round piping tip (tip #12 ~8mm, or something close to it). Load the macronage in and pipe onto the sheet. If you’ve never done this, I suggest you watch a video. Slam the tray on the counter a couple of times to help flattening the macarons and to get rid of air bubbles. You can also use a toothpick to pop any bubbles that stay after this, and smooth the aftermath of said bubbles.
If your macarons have tips, you’ve undermixed the macronage. Dip your finger in water and gently pat them down. If your macarons spread a lot, the macronage is overmixed and there’s no fixing it.
Stick some elderflower blooms (without the green parts, just the tiny blossoms) on about half of the shells. Let the shells sit for 30-60min, until they develop a skin and are no longer sticky. Preheat the oven to 135°C.
Bake for 23 minutes, rotating halfway through. Longer on a silicone mat. Let them cool completely on the mats.

Notes

Tried adding elderflowers into the granulated sugar, letting sit overnight and using in the meringue, but there was no noticable taste. Lime zest should work instead, to be tried.
It is highly recommended you use a kitchen robot for the meringue.
This amount will make 2-3 baking trays.

Assembly

Match the macaron shells so you have pairs of similar size. Put the ganache into a piping bag with a smaller tip and pipe a ring of the ganache on the macaron. Put the strawberry reduction in the ring and top with another shell.
Let them rest in your fridge until the shells can absorb the moisture from the filling. Or be a goblin and eat them right away.
